key_takeaways: Vietnamese law provides for marriage registration by foreigners residing in Vietnam. Two non-resident Australians should get written confirmation from the provincial Department of Justice first.
Since 1 July 2025, commune or ward People's Committees register marriages involving foreigners: 5 working days from a complete dossier, up to 10 with verification.
Australians need a Certificate of No Impediment to Marriage (CNI). DFAT in Australia charges AUD 181 (2026 fee); the Ho Chi Minh City Consulate-General issues it next working day.
Vietnam's apostille rules took effect on 11 September 2026, but Smartraveller still describes embassy authentication. Ask the registering office which it accepts before ordering anything.
Marrying legally in Australia (NOIM at least one month ahead) and celebrating in Vietnam removes the CNI, legalisation, translations and People's Committee registration.

faq.q: Can foreigners get married in Vietnam?
faq.a: Vietnam's Law on Civil Status provides for registration where a foreigner residing in Vietnam asks to marry, and for a Vietnamese citizen marrying a foreigner. The Australian Consulate-General in Ho Chi Minh City confirms that Australians must submit a CNI. Residence is the question to settle first.

faq.q: Can two Australians get married in Vietnam without a Vietnamese partner?
faq.a: Only if the authorities confirm it. The law ties registration between foreigners to residence in Vietnam, and Decree 120/2025 sends requests from people with no residence to the provincial Department of Justice. Get that office's answer in writing before you plan a legal ceremony.

faq.q: Is a marriage in Vietnam legally recognised in Australia?
faq.a: Smartraveller says an overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia but in most cases is recognised if it was valid where it took place and would have been valid under Australian law. The certificate is usually accepted as proof, but may not be enough for a change of name.

faq.q: When is the best time of year for a destination wedding in Vietnam?
faq.a: Smartraveller notes that Vietnam's storm season usually runs from June to November, with heavy rain, floods and typhoons that can affect flights, roads and power. We cannot promise weather in any month; whatever date you choose, build in a wet-weather plan and flexible travel.

faq.q: Do our Australian guests need a visa for Vietnam?
faq.a: Yes, a visa or a visa exemption certificate. Smartraveller says Australians cannot get a visa on arrival; the tourism eVisa, if granted, may allow up to 90 days. Guests should apply only through the official eVisa website and carry a printed copy.
